Mina: Quick flag from the streaming loader spikes this morning - long-tail resumes are failing checksum validation about 1/500 reads when using range requests against gzipped safetensors bundles.
Felix: ouch. is it a server-side chunk boundary mismatch or our reassembly?
Mina: reassembly seems fine locally. failing cases show a 1-2 byte shift in the final block, checksum mismatch from client side only after resume.
Diego: could be double-compressed segments when upstream gateway does on-the-fly gzip. We do range on the compressed blob, which means byte-range boundaries don't map to uncompressed frames.
Mina: exactly. repro steps: 1) request bytes 10m-12m of file.gz 2) loader decompresses slice -> invalid trailing bits -> checksum fail.
Felix: two high-level fixes: A) prefer server-side support for ranged DECOMPRESSED segments (requires origin change), or B) attach a streaming resume token to manifest that encodes uncompressed offset and CRC so client can request proper boundaries.
Diego: B seems less invasive upstream. Proposed manifest addition:
```
stream_resume_tokens:
  - shard: weights-0001.safetensors.gz
    token: "v1:crc32:1234abcd:uncompressed_offset:1048576"
    length: 1048576
```
QA-bot: note: token must be integrity protected and signed if we allow cross-region caches to rely on it.
Mina: plus loader change: when we see a token, use GET with range on compressed that aligns with token.range_hint, then decompress and verify CRC before merging. If CRC fails, fall back to full-file fetch.
Felix: need to define token semantics: 1) authoritative uncompressed offset mapping, 2) recomputable CRC (crc32 or adler32 but prefer crc32c), 3) opaque signature to guard tampering.
Diego: implementation detail: add LoaderAPI method `ResumeParse(token)` that returns an idempotent reader. Also update prefetcher to store `resume_token` in in-memory slab metadata so eviction/resume can coordinate.
Mina: tradeoffs: token approach increases manifest size but avoids origin changes. downside: clients must trust token mapping and there's a potential for stale tokens if upstream recompresses.
Felix: mitigation: token TTL in manifest and `token_version` field. If token_version mismatches, loader falls back to full fetch.
Diego: also add a small compatibility shim: if manifest is missing token, we fallback to current behavior (full fetch on resume). Backward compatibility preserved.
QA-bot: test plan: fuzzed resume rounds, cross-region recompress scenarios, and corrupted-token injection tests.
infra-bot: rolling digest: schedule origin-gateway consult for ranged-decompress support.
Mina: action items: 1) Diego to PR manifest schema + sample tokens (2 days). 2) Felix to add ResumeParse and metadata hook in loader (3 days). 3) QA to add fuzz harness (1 day). 4) Ops to probe origin for ranged-decompress (async).
Felix: also propose telemetry metrics: resume_success_rate, resume_crc_failures, resume_fallbacks_full_fetch.
Diego: I'll include a short note in RFC #527: "stream-resume-tokens" with schema and security considerations.
Mina: cool. for now I'll disable the aggressive resume path for gzipped bundles until tokens land.
Felix: thanks, good call.
QA-bot: test matrix item created: ENGML-4321.
Mina: wrapping up - will drop a link to the PR in this thread.
